***XXL*** is an American [hip hop](Hip_hop_culture "Hip hop culture") [magazine](Magazine "Magazine"), published by [Townsquare Media](Townsquare_Media "Townsquare Media"), founded in 1997.

## History

In August 1997,[[1]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-1) [Harris Publications](Harris_Publications "Harris Publications") released the first issue of *XXL*. It featured rappers <Jay-Z> and [Master P](Master_P "Master P") on a double cover.[[2]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-xxlmag1-2) In December 2006, *XXL* took over the struggling hip-hop producer and DJ magazine *[Scratch](Scratch_(magazine) "Scratch (magazine)")* (another publication owned by Harris Publications), re-branding it as *XXL Presents Scratch Magazine*. However *Scratch* shut down less than a year later in September 2007.

Other titles with limited runs have been launched under the *XXL* brand, including *Hip-Hop Soul*, *Eye Candy* and *[Shade45](Shade_45 "Shade 45")*. *XXL* has released many other special projects including tour programs, mixtapes and exclusive DVDs. *XXL* also maintains a popular website, which provides daily hip hop news, original content and content from the magazine.[[3]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-3)

In 2014, [Townsquare Media](Townsquare_Media "Townsquare Media") acquired *XXL*,[[4]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-bill-4) *[King](King_(magazine) "King (magazine)")* and *Antenna* from Harris Publications.

On October 14, 2014, Townsquare announced it would continue print publication of *XXL*.[[5]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-5) In December 2014 the company reported that the magazine would be published on a monthly basis.[[4]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-bill-4)

### Past editors

The magazine's past editors include Reginald C. Dennis (formerly of *[The Source](The_Source_(magazine) "The Source (magazine)")*), Sheena Lester (former editor-in-chief of *RapPages* and *[Vibe](Vibe_(magazine) "Vibe (magazine)")* music editor), Elliott Wilson (formerly of The Beat-Down Newspaper, *[ego trip](Ego_trip_(magazine) "Ego trip (magazine)")* and *The Source,* currently locked in at #7 slot on The Source's Digital 30 list.)[[6]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-6)[[7]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-7) and Datwon Thomas (former editor-in-chief of *[King](King_(magazine) "King (magazine)"))*.

In May 2009, Datwon Thomas resigned from *XXL* and executive editor Vanessa Satten, who had been with *XXL* since 1998, was named the new Editor-in-Chief.[[8]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-8)

### Special releases

In August 2005, <Eminem> and *XXL* teamed up to release a special issue titled *XXL Presents Shade 45*, designed to simultaneously give maximum exposure to his [radio station](Radio_station "Radio station") [Shade 45](Shade_45 "Shade 45"), the station's associated radio [DJs](Disc_jockey "Disc jockey"), the [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records") label as a whole, and [G-Unit Records](G-Unit_Records "G-Unit Records")' artists. *XXL* executive publisher Jonathan Rheingold stated that typically magazines based around particular artists were not favorable, but "since Shade 45 is a truly authentic and uncensored rap radio channel, the marriage with the *XXL* brand made sense," feeling that it would interest rap fans.[[9]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-9)

In November 2008, *XXL* released *XXL Raps Volume 1*, which included music from [50 Cent](50_Cent "50 Cent"), <G-Unit>, [Common](Common_(rapper) "Common (rapper)"), [Jim Jones](Jim_Jones_(rapper) "Jim Jones (rapper)"), & <Fabolous>.[[10]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-10)

In September 2006, *XXL* put a special 90-minute DVD called *XXL DVD Magazine Vol. 1*, which featured exclusive interviews and content with big-name rappers such as [50 Cent](50_Cent "50 Cent"), [Ice Cube](Ice_Cube "Ice Cube"), [Fat Joe](Fat_Joe "Fat Joe"), [Paul Wall](Paul_Wall "Paul Wall"), & [Mike Jones](Mike_Jones_(rapper) "Mike Jones (rapper)").[[11]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-11)

On August 20, 2013, *XXL* marked its sixteenth anniversary by releasing its 150th issue, which featured the first solo cover on the magazine from [Drake](Drake_(rapper) "Drake (rapper)"), along with rappers such as [Kendrick Lamar](Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") and <B.o.B> reviewing classic albums.[[2]](XXL_(magazine)#cite_note-xxlmag1-2)
